question: What is the main reason nurses document patient care?

options.A: To record patient care and clinical responses
options.B: To calculate daily patient hospital bills
options.D: To evaluate hospital staff performance ratings

explanation: Documentation is all about keeping a clear timeline of how the patient is doing and what care was given! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h1)

question: Why is good documentation so important for the whole healthcare team?

options.A: It prevents patients from asking questions about treatment
options.B: It ensures continuity of care across different shifts
options.C: It dictates the exact salary of each attending doctor
options.D: It removes the need for physical patient assessments

explanation: When different shifts take over, shared records make sure everyone knows what has already been done for the patient. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h1)

question: If a legal issue arises, how do patient records act in court?

options.A: As a waiver for patient consent
options.B: As legal evidence of care given
options.C: As a guarantee of zero medical errors
options.D: As proof of the doctor's personal income

explanation: Remember, your chart speaks for you in court! It proves the exact treatments and care that were provided. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h2)

question: How do patient records help hospitals improve the quality of their care?

options.A: They determine the interior design of the ward
options.B: They supply data for clinical audits and reviews
options.C: They set the working hours for administrative staff
options.D: They replace the need for hospital equipment maintenance

explanation: Hospitals review charts during clinical audits to see how well safety standards are being met. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h2)

question: In the eyes of the law and nursing practice, what does unrecorded care mean?

options.A: It is assumed another ward handled it
options.B: It automatically doubles the patient bill
options.C: It is legally considered care not done
options.D: It requires a formal apology to the family

explanation: If you didn't write it down, legally, it never happened! Always make it a habit to chart promptly. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h3)

question: Which of these charting habits is a serious professional and legal violation?

options.B: Writing the exact time an injection was given
options.C: Using black ink for all handwritten notes
options.D: Backdating or altering previous nursing entries

explanation: Falsifying or tampering with medical records messes with your professional integrity and is a big legal no-no. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h3)

question: Which of these examples is a clear, objective nursing entry?

options.B: Patient slept like a baby all night

explanation: Objective data is based on facts and measurable numbers, not vague opinions like 'looks better' or 'slept like a baby'. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h4)

question: Why is it a bad idea to record a nursing procedure before you actually do it?

options.A: It falsifies the timeline and compromises patient safety
options.B: It confuses the pharmacist dispensing medications
options.C: It uses up too much space on the paper chart
options.D: It increases the cost of hospital consumables

explanation: Never chart ahead of time! Plans can change unexpectedly, and your records must always match reality. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h4)

question: In the SOAP charting format, what does the letter 'P' stand for?
explanation: SOAP is a classic format standing for Subjective, Objective, Assessment, and Plan. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h5)

question: What is the main idea behind Charting by Exception (CBE)?

options.A: Doctors write all the nursing notes for the shift
options.B: Patients document their own vital signs daily
options.C: Only abnormal findings or deviations are documented
options.D: Every single routine bath is written in full detail

explanation: CBE saves time by assuming standard routine care was done unless you write down an exception. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h5)

question: What does the letter 'S' stand for at the very start of the ISBAR reporting tool?
explanation: ISBAR starts strong with Introduction and Situation so everyone knows the immediate problem right away. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h6)

question: Why do nurses use a structured handover tool like ISBAR during shift changes?

options.A: It prevents critical patient details from being forgotten
options.B: It stops patients from asking about their discharge
options.C: It shortens the working hours of incoming nurses
options.D: It eliminates the need for written patient records

explanation: A structured format keeps your handover organized so no important patient details slip through the cracks. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h6)

question: If a patient has a fall, where should you document the incident report?

options.A: In the personal diary of the ward manager
options.B: On a separate administrative incident form
options.C: Inside the patient's permanent clinical chart
options.D: On the public notice board of the hospital

explanation: Incident reports are kept separate from the main medical chart as part of internal hospital safety tracking. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h7)

question: Why must you NOT mention the incident report inside the patient's regular nursing notes?

options.A: To prevent the report from being used as routine trial evidence
options.B: To save space for daily vital sign recordings
options.C: To speed up the patient discharge process
options.D: To hide mistakes from the hospital management team

explanation: Keeping incident reports separate protects internal quality safety reviews from automatic legal discovery. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h7)

question: What is the proper way to fix a mistake when writing in a paper nursing chart?

options.A: Scratch it out aggressively until it is unreadable
options.B: Draw a single line through it and sign
options.C: Tear out the entire page and rewrite the notes
options.D: Cover the mistake completely with correction fluid

explanation: Just draw one clean line through the error so the original words can still be seen, then sign and date it! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h8)

question: Which of these is considered bad practice when charting?

options.A: Using approved hospital abbreviations in notes
options.B: Signing your full signature and rank after an entry
options.C: Writing entries immediately after completing a procedure
options.D: Documenting care given by another nurse before they arrive

explanation: Always stick to documenting only the care that you personally performed and witnessed yourself. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h8)
